title: JBL Cinema SB510 3.1 Channel Soundbar with Built-in Subwoofer $149 Delivered Only @ Telstra
body:
Deal: JBL Cinema SB510 3.1 Channel Soundbar with Built-in Subwoofer $149 Delivered Only @ Telstra

[Shekster] Just be aware that unless you really need one right now, this has been significantly cheaper on multiple occasions , and is not a new model either.
Decent cheap soundbar which will be an upgrade over most inbuilt speakers on modern TVs (which are now funnily enough significantly worse in quality compared to old TVs due to how slim/compact TVs are becoming which limits the quality of audio which can be physically generated within. Currently use this with a TCL C8K. Would definitely recommend it if drops back down to the ~$100 mark again
[jmc787] Yeah Telstra normally only discounts ancient stuff that has gathered a thick layer of dust in their warehouse.
[shutuptakemymoney101] When has ever 'needing one' been a reason not to buy a bargain? :-)
Thanks OP.
[Shekster] Tbf the point being made was that it isn't really a bargain, and as such if you don't "need one", then it doesn't really make sense to buy it at a price significantly above what it has been in the past…
Definitely a solid deal though if you actually did need a soundbar :-) Thanks OP!
[Blitzfx] The treble on these are really bad. The bass is decent, and better than a few TVs. You get what you pay for even at $150. I would wait for it to be cheaper.
[Iggemo] It's pretty good. Be aware the 3.1 is a bit of an issue. I've written to JBL about it and they've been no help at all. In theory what should happen, say, with 5.1 content is it should downmix successfully to 3.1, but ive found in multiple media players this doesnt happen, leading to some bizarre results. For example, when you play a South Park episode, there's no music during the intro, only vocals - things along that line. Missing channels seems to be a big issue. I've resorted to just PCM;ing all audio meaning, in effect, it's basically a 2.1 anyway since the 3.1 is completely unreliable. That's been my experience, anyway.
[munnamirjan] If you can price match with good guys plus use this it might bit cheaper .
[munnamirjan] Plus, there was a $40 voucher sent via message for a $150 purchase, which expires tomorrow. If you can combine the price beat + $40 voucher + the voucher from the above offer, the final price should come down to less than $100.
I did something similar when I purchased the Motorola Edge and managed to get it under $305:
Price beat with Dick Smith: $547 vs. $599
AGL Good Guys voucher: $150
$40 voucher from message
$20 Gold Member voucher
10% off from the above offer
So, if you can combine these offers in a similar way, then it should be good .
Plus you will get 40$ gift card offer . Here is the this
[frank100] recently bought it for 220$ it is not as good as the description claims
The tremble and bass are horrible, I agree with the above comments
I connected with mobile bluetooth it was making strange noise
[theodosius] Turn the bass to the lowest setting and it sounds good
[Overcomerak] Is this better than the Harman Kardon Aura 4?
